CPT10303.name: The Philosophy and Ethics of Biology

PCC12803.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences

componentContentNotes.y1-bioorganic: Introduces biomolecular structure, reactivity, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms and molecular interactions through lectures, exercises and practical work.
componentContentNotes.y1-ecology1: Introduces ecological theories and principles through research and applications in nature management, agriculture, fisheries and environmental policy.
componentContentNotes.y1-ecology2: Complements Ecology I with data-generating field, greenhouse or laboratory investigations, a literature-based project proposal, reports and a presentation.
componentContentNotes.y1-cell: Studies plant, animal and bacterial cells, organelles, cellular organisation, differentiation and communication, with practical investigation and group discussion.
componentContentNotes.y1-analysis: Develops differentiation, integration and simple first-order differential equations for scientific applications.
componentContentNotes.y1-chem: Studies molecular interactions, energy exchange, thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, buffers and reaction kinetics in living systems.
componentContentNotes.y1-genetics: Develops inheritance, chromosome mapping, gene expression, genomics, gene manipulation, population genetics and complex traits.
componentContentNotes.y1-evolution: Studies evolutionary mechanisms within populations and species, selection, speciation, the history of life and comparative methods.
componentContentNotes.y1-zoology: Studies vertebrate structure and function, development and evolutionary adaptations through comparative anatomy and laboratory investigation.
componentContentNotes.y1-plants: Connects plant cells, tissues and whole-plant structure to development, photosynthesis, transport, growth regulation and interactions with microorganisms.
componentContentNotes.y1-biodiversity: Practises identification of Dutch plants and animals, diagnostic keys, field observations and biodiversity comparisons across habitats.
componentContentNotes.y1-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentContentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentContentNotes.y2-physics: Applies optics, mechanics, fluid flow, diffusion, heat and other physical principles to biological phenomena.
componentContentNotes.y2-reproduction: Studies plant reproductive strategies, flowering, fertilisation, embryogenesis, seeds and fruits, with practical investigation of structure and development.
componentContentNotes.y2-physiology: Connects mammalian organ systems, morphology, physiological regulation and environmental adaptation through practical work and a case study.
componentContentNotes.y2-modelling: Uses mathematical and computational models to turn biological hypotheses into predictions that can be investigated and tested.
componentContentNotes.y2-microbio: Studies the genetic, physiological, morphological and ecological diversity of microorganisms, supported by practical investigation.
componentContentNotes.y2-ethics: Examines how biology explains phenomena and informs social, animal, environmental and biotechnology ethics.
componentContentNotes.y2-development: Studies molecular mechanisms of plant and animal development, including differential gene expression, stem cells, communication and pattern formation.
componentContentNotes.y2-behaviour: Uses Tinbergen’s four questions to study animal behaviour, with practical data collection and analysis, study design and scientific writing.
componentContentNotes.y2-diversityskills: Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.
componentContentNotes.y3-advancedstats: Six-credit compulsory study of regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, using R. The thesis module’s Ecological Methods alternative does not remove this programme requirement.
componentContentNotes.y1-mathchoice: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.
componentContentNotes.y2-specialisation: Illustrative restricted option for a cellular, plant or animal direction: laboratory and computational investigation of DNA, RNA and proteins, including cloning, PCR, protein analysis and enzyme kinetics. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. Final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified.
componentContentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 24-credit laboratory, field or data-science/modelling research generating new data, with a plan, scientific article, presentations and defence. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising chair. Their current allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project at least four months beforehand.
componentContentNotes.y3-ro3: Choose at least 12 credits from the prescribed RO3 list and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising thesis chair. Some listed courses carry three credits, so the credit minimum and two-course condition must both be met. This reserved block is not a verified combination.
componentContentNotes.y3-choice: Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses.

mandatoryAndAdvisoryFindings: General/Laboratory/Fieldwork Safety remain0EC; relevant lab/field modules explicitly require these. EcologyII complements/runs alongside EcologyI. MathIntroduction/VWO-B supports Analysis/LinearAlgebra, Stats2 supportsAdvancedStats, firstyear math/ecology/stats/physics supportsBiologicalModels. Cell/organismal/chemistry foundations support Genetics,Physiology,Microbiology,Plants,Reproduction andDevelopment; BIC10306 assumesCell/Microbiology and LabSafety. EZO23809 P5 must precedeP6/fieldpart. Currentcommon AdvancedStats6 remainscompulsory despite thesis AK alternative. Advisory knowledge is not silently promoted into a new mandatory gate.
